findings.text: Condition `[ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]` is inverted - default packages only install when prior command FAILED. Also EXIT_CODE is uninitialized here (declaration moved but initialization removed), causing undefined behavior. Input: successful nvm use with SKIP_DEFAULT_PACKAGES unset will skip default packages.

Condition `[ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]` prevents reinstall-packages from running on success. The reinstall should happen when installation succeeds, not fails. Input: installing a version with REINSTALL_PACKAGES_FROM set will skip reinstalling packages.
Condition `[ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]` prevents alias from being set on success. Alias should be set when installation succeeds. Input: installing with ALIAS set will fail to create the alias.

Returns uninitialized EXIT_CODE variable instead of actual command result. The initialization `EXIT_CODE=-1` was removed but variable is still returned, causing unpredictable return values. Input: any install path returns garbage exit code.

In nvm_install_default_packages, if nvm_get_default_packages succeeds but returns empty string, function returns 0 (success code) instead of continuing. The condition `[ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ] || [ -z "${DEFAULT_PACKAGES}" ]` returns early on empty packages with wrong exit code.

3.reason: The finding describes the same root cause as the reference bug: the EXIT_CODE variable is used uninitialized in the already-installed branch, causing default-packages, reinstall-packages, and alias steps to be gated on the inverted test.
